full_text_en:
Beijing Baidu Netcom Science Technology Co., Ltd. v. Qingdao Aoshang Network Technology Co., Ltd., Qingdao Branch of China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., Shandong Branch of China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., and Qingdao Pengfei International Aviation Travel Service Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Unfair Competition

【Ruling Summary】

I. The existence of a competitive relationship between market entities is not limited to whether they belong to the same industry or category of services. If there is a certain connection between the two in market competition, or if one party's conduct improperly hinders the other party's legitimate business activities and damages its lawful rights and interests, a competitive relationship between them should be affirmed. Providing Internet access services and providing search services are different types of network services. However, where an Internet access service provider, by taking advantage of its condition of providing Internet access services, either alone or jointly with other network service providers, artificially interferes with the search requests of its service targets, and forcibly pops up advertising pages that are closely related to the searched keywords and content before the search results appear, such interference is aimed at profiting from the service provider's search service conduct for its own benefit. It is likely to cause network users to mistakenly believe that the forcibly popped-up advertising pages were published by the search service provider, affects the quality of the search service provider's services, damages its lawful rights and interests, and violates the principle of good faith and recognized business ethics. According to the fundamental provisions of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, such conduct shall be deemed to constitute unfair competition.

II. In determining the infringer in a network infringement case, ascertaining the facts of network technology is a prerequisite for legal judgment. In this process, special attention should be paid to fully leveraging the role of technical expert witnesses in the network field and reasonably applying the rules on the burden of proof to identify the infringer.

Plaintiff: Beijing Baidu Netcom Science Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. [Address], North Fourth Ring West Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Liang Zhixiang, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Qingdao Aoshang Network Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. [Address], Ningxia Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Guan Wu, Manager of the company.

Defendant: Qingdao Branch of China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. [Address], Yan'an Third Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Representative: Liu Dehai, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Shandong Branch of China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. [Address], Jingsan Road, Jinan, Shandong Province.

Representative: Huo Haifeng, General Manager of the company.

Third Party: Qingdao Pengfei International Aviation Travel Service Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. [Address], Ningxia Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Li Zongshi, General Manager of the company.

The Plaintiff, Beijing Baidu Netcom Science Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baidu Company), filed a lawsuit with the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court against the Defendants, Qingdao Aoshang Network Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aoshang Network Company), the Qingdao Branch of China United Network Communications Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Unicom Qingdao Company), the Shandong Branch of China United Network Communications Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Unicom Shandong Company), and the Third Party, Qingdao Pengfei International Aviation Travel Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pengfei Aviation Company), regarding a dispute over unfair competition.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The Plaintiff is a leading domestic manufacturer of Chinese-language search engine technology. The website www.baidu.com owned by the Plaintiff is the world's largest Chinese-language search engine website, with over 100 million netizens visiting the Baidu website and querying information daily. Through investigation, the Plaintiff learned that the Defendants, Aoshang Network Company, Unicom Qingdao Company, and Unicom Shandong Company, utilized the Internet access network services of China Netcom in the Qingdao area to forcibly add advertisements on the Plaintiff's search results pages for promotional purposes. This prevented the Plaintiff from providing services normally to Internet users, caused a large number of netizens to mistakenly believe that the advertisements placed by the three Defendants were intentionally set by the Plaintiff, greatly damaged the Plaintiff's business operation model, harmed the reputation and corporate goodwill of the Plaintiff's search services, and resulted in a significant loss of netizens and traffic. At the same time, this conduct severely weakened the Plaintiff's competitiveness as a search engine marketing service provider, diverted a large number of the Plaintiff's existing and potential customers, caused a substantial loss of customers for the Plaintiff, and directly damaged the Plaintiff's economic benefits. The conduct of the three Defendants violated the market conduct principles of good faith and fair dealing and constituted serious unfair competition. Therefore, the Plaintiff requested the court to: 1. Declare that the conduct of Aoshang Network Company and Unicom Qingdao Company constituted unfair competition against the Plaintiff and order them to cease such unfair competitive conduct; order Unicom Shandong Company to bear joint and several liability within the scope of its legal responsibilities; 2. Order the three Defendants to publish statements in *People's Daily*, *Legal Daily*, *Peninsula City News*, and *Qingdao Evening News* to eliminate the adverse effects; 3. Order the three Defendants to jointly compensate the Plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 4.8 million; 4. Order the three Defendants to bear the Plaintiff's reasonable expenses incurred in connection with this case, including attorney fees, notarization fees, and travel expenses, totaling RMB 100,000.

Defendant Aoshang Network Company's Defense: Aoshang Network Company did not engage in any unfair competition conduct. Even if such conduct existed, it should not be required to apologize. Even if an apology were warranted, it should not be published in *Legal Daily*. The Plaintiff, Baidu Company, failed to provide strong evidence to support its claim for compensation of RMB 4.8 million.

Defendant Unicom Qingdao Company's Defense: The Plaintiff's allegations were based on speculation and unfounded presumptions. The evidence submitted by the Plaintiff could not necessarily, definitively, or exclusively demonstrate that the Defendants had engaged in, or how they had engaged in, the conduct alleged. The Plaintiff did not submit any new evidence to prove the actual losses it suffered as a result of the alleged conduct of the Defendants. Requested the court to dismiss all of the Plaintiff's claims.

Defendant Unicom Shandong Company's Defense: The Plaintiff, Baidu Company, did not provide any valid evidence to prove that Unicom Shandong Company had engaged in the alleged unfair competition or infringement conduct. The Plaintiff's statements regarding the legal relationship between the Defendants Unicom Qingdao Company and Unicom Shandong Company were inconsistent with the facts and lacked legal basis.

Third Party Pengfei Aviation Company's Defense: The Third Party is unrelated to this case. The Plaintiff, Baidu Company, brought a malicious lawsuit causing reputational damage and economic losses, including attorney fees, to the Third Party. The Third Party reserves the right to file a lawsuit.

The Qingdao Intermediate People's Court found the following facts at first instance:

The Plaintiff, Baidu Company, was established on June 5, 2001. Its business scope includes Internet information services. Approved by the Beijing Communications Administration, it operates the Baidu website at www.baidu.com, which primarily provides Internet information search services to netizens and is currently a well-known search engine website in China.

The Defendant, Aoshang Network Company, was established on September 22, 2003. Its business scope includes network engineering construction, network technology application services, computer software design and development, etc. Its website is www.og.com.cn. On the "Company Overview" page of this website, the company states that it owns four websites: China Aoshang Net (www.og.com.cn), Ouge Network Marketing Partner (www.og.net.cn), Qingdao Telephone Real-Name Net (www.0532114.org), and Peninsula Talent Net (www.job17.com). On the same website, when introducing its "Network Express" service, the company states: "No plug-in installation required, advertising pages appear forcibly." When introducing the "Search Pass" product's presentation format, it lists the following steps using text and images: Step 1: Enter keywords in the search engine dialog box; Step 2: The Network Express advertisement slot appears first (displayed for 5 seconds); Step 3: Clicking on the above advertisement slot directly opens a new window to the promotional website; Step 4: After 5 seconds, the original window automatically displays the search results for the initial request. The website also introduces the above services in other forms.

The Defendant, Unicom Qingdao Company, was established on October 24, 2008, following the merger of the former Qingdao Branch of China Netcom and the former Qingdao Branch of China Unicom. Unicom Qingdao Company's business scope includes Internet access services and information services, among others. The Qingdao Information Port website (domain name qd.sd.cn) is owned by Unicom Qingdao Company. "Telephone Real-Name" is a voice search service jointly operated by Unicom Qingdao Company and the Defendant Aoshang Company. The website at www.0532114.org, titled "114 Telephone Real-Name Voice Search," indicates that the copyright owner of the website is Unicom Qingdao Company, and the exclusive registration center is Aoshang Network Company.

The Defendant, Unicom Shandong Company, was also established following the merger of related companies, with an approval date of March 11, 2009. Its business scope also includes Internet access services and information services. The website of Unicom Shandong Company (www.sdcnc.cn) shows that the Defendant Unicom Qingdao Company is its subordinate branch.

The Third Party, Pengfei Aviation Company, was established on June 14, 2002. Its business scope includes air ticket sales agency services, among others.

On April 14, 2009, the Shinan Notary Public Office of Qingdao City, Shandong Province, issued Notarial Certificate No. (2009) Qing Shizhong Zheng Min Zi No. 002187, notarizing the process of the Plaintiff's authorized agent using a computer at the notary office to log in to Baidu and other websites. The main contents of this notarial certificate are as follows:

1. Logged in to www.ip138.com; the website displayed the IP address of the networked computer as 221.3.38.111; querying the geographic location of this address showed: Primary data: China Netcom, Qingdao, Shandong; Reference data 1: China Netcom, Qingdao, Shandong; Reference data 2: China Netcom Qingdao ADSL, Shandong.

2. Logged in to the Baidu website (www.baidu.com), searched for the free network protocol detection program software "wireshark," followed the link provided by the Baidu website to a website named "Sea Software Garden" (www.softsea.net), downloaded a program named "wireshark-win32-1.1.2.exe," and installed it on the computer.

3. Logged in to the Baidu website (www.baidu.com), entered "Pengfei Aviation" in the dialog box displayed on the website, clicked "Baidu Search," and a page displaying "Get Discounted Tickets First, Just Dial 114" popped up. This page then redirected to the corresponding "Pengfei Aviation" search results page.

4. Logged in to the Baidu website (www.baidu.com), entered "Aviation Ticketing" in the dialog box displayed on the website, operated the "wireshark-win32-1.1.2.exe" program, and generated a background log file.

5. Logged in to the Baidu website (www.baidu.com), entered "Pengfei Aviation" in the dialog box displayed on the website, clicked "Baidu Search," and a page displaying "Get Discounted Tickets First, Just Dial 114" popped up. Quickly clicking on this page, which displayed "Get Discounted Tickets First, Just Dial 114," opened a page showing the address http://air.qd.sd.cn. The "wireshark-win32-1.1.2.exe" program was operated to generate a background log file.

On the same day, the Shinan Notary Public Office of Qingdao City issued Notarial Certificate No. (2009) Qing Shizhong Zheng Min Zi No. 002188, notarizing the process of the Plaintiff's authorized agent using a computer at the notary office to log in to Baidu and other websites. The main contents of this notarial certificate are as follows:

Logged in to the Baidu website (www.baidu.com), entered "Qingdao Talent Net" in the dialog box displayed on the website, clicked "Baidu Search," and a page displaying "Find Good Jobs at Peninsula Talent Net www.job17.com" popped up. Quickly clicking on the "Click Now" displayed on this page opened a page showing the address http://www.job17.com/.

Logged in to the Baidu website (www.baidu.com), entered "Telephone Real-Name" in the dialog box displayed on the website, clicked "Baidu Search," and a page displaying "Get Info, Dial 114, Voice Search is More Convenient" popped up. This page then redirected to the corresponding "Telephone Real-Name" search results page.

Regarding the fact that within the network signal of the Defendant Unicom Qingdao Company, entering corresponding keywords on the Baidu website would cause related advertising pages to pop up, the Plaintiff Baidu Company, in the capacity of an expert, conducted the following analysis of the page visit records and corresponding background files recorded in Notarial Certificate No. (2009) Qing Shizhong Zheng Min Zi No. 002187: 1. The main tools used were a data packet analysis tool (wireshark-setup-0.99.6a.exe), the ping command included with Windows, the IP address information query service provided by www.ip138.com, and the whois domain name information query service provided by whois.webmasterhome.cn; 2. The conclusions were: (1) Data packet No. 56 was suspicious; the HTML code transmitted in this data packet would cause the following result: display an advertisement in the user's browser (http://61.156.12.58/webts/cnc/114dingpiao1/index.htmL), and after eight seconds, resend the search request previously made by the user to Baidu; (2) Based on publicly available query information, the URL address pointed to by the source link of the frame (http://61.156.12.58/webts/cnc/114dingpiao1/index.htmL) was linked to a website (http://air.qd.sd.cn/) that shared the same domain (qd.sd.cn) as the website of the Defendant Unicom Shandong Company's subordinate site — Qingdao Information Port (www.qd.sd.cn); (3) According to the principle of the same domain, the website http://air.qd.sd.cn belonged to the Qingdao site subordinate to Unicom Shandong Company.

None of the Defendants, Aoshang Network Company, Unicom Qingdao Company, and Unicom Shandong Company, raised any substantive objections to the authenticity of the above expert opinion and the *Background File* preserved by the notarial certificate.

The issues in dispute at the first instance of this case were: I. Whether the Defendants, Aoshang Network Company, Unicom Qingdao Company, and Unicom Shandong Company, engaged in the conduct of forcibly popping up relevant advertising pages when a search was performed on the Plaintiff Baidu Company's search engine website; II. If the Defendants did engage in the above conduct, whether such conduct constituted unfair competition.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Qingdao Intermediate People's Court):

I. Regarding whether the Defendants, Aoshang Network Company, Unicom Qingdao Company, and Unicom Shandong Company, engaged in the conduct alleged by the Plaintiff Baidu Company.

It can be seen from the facts found in this case that during the process of applying for evidence preservation by the Shinan Notary Public Office of Qingdao City, the Plaintiff Baidu Company logged in to the Plaintiff's search website www.baidu.com through the Internet access service provided by the Defendant Unicom Qingdao Company. When "Pengfei Aviation" was entered in the dialog box displayed on the Baidu website, a page displaying "Get Discounted Tickets First, Just Dial 114" would pop up. Clicking this page would open a page showing the address http://air.qd.sd.cn. When "Qingdao Talent Net" was entered in the dialog box displayed on the Baidu website, a page displaying "Find Good Jobs at Peninsula Talent Net www.job17.com" would pop up. Clicking this page would open a page showing the address http://www.job17.com/. When "Telephone Real-Name" was entered in the dialog box displayed on the Baidu website and "Baidu Search" was clicked, a page displaying "Get Info, Dial 114, Voice Search is More Convenient" would pop up, followed by a redirection to the corresponding "Telephone Real-Name" search results page.

Based on the facts found, www.job17.com is the Peninsula Talent website owned by the Defendant Aoshang Network Company, and "Telephone Real-Name Voice Search" is a business operated jointly by the Defendant Unicom Qingdao Company and Aoshang Network Company. The parties have no objection to this. The dispute among the parties in this case concerns whether the website with IP address http://air.qd.sd.cn belongs to Unicom Qingdao Company. In this regard, the court of first instance holds: First, the parties have no objection that the domain name qd.sd.cn belongs to Unicom Qingdao Company, and Unicom Qingdao Company actually uses it as the domain name for "Qingdao Information Port." Second, a complete domain name consists of two or more parts, separated by English periods ".". The part to the right of the last "." is called the top-level domain (TLD), the part to the left of the last "." is called the second-level domain, the part to the left of the second-level domain is called the third-level domain, and so on. Therefore, http://air.qd.sd.cn is a subdomain of qd.sd.cn. Third, although Unicom Qingdao Company submitted a printout of the webpage qdmuh.qd.sd.cn to argue that subdomains under qd.sd.cn are not necessarily owned by it, Unicom Qingdao Company avoided the issue that, as the owner of the domain name qd.sd.cn, the acquisition of subdomains under that domain requires its permission. According to the general rules of domain name naming, each level of domain controls the allocation of its lower-level subdomains. Although the domain name holder and the user of a subdomain may not be the same civil subject, unless the domain name holder transfers its subdomain for use by others, it is impossible for others to use the domain name holder's subdomain through legitimate means. Unicom Qingdao Company did not provide any contrary evidence to refute this. As the holder of the domain name qd.sd.cn, Unicom Qingdao Company was capable of identifying the actual user of the http://air.qd.sd.cn domain name at the time of the Plaintiff's notarial preservation, but it failed to provide such explanation. Therefore, it should be determined that the user of this subdomain at the time of the Plaintiff's notarial preservation was Unicom Qingdao Company.

When a user logs into a search engine website to conduct a keyword search on the Internet, what normally appears should be the search results page of the search engine website, and no other pages unrelated to the search engine website should pop up. However, within the network access service area provided by the defendant China Unicom Qingdao Branch, there appeared a phenomenon where advertisement pages unrelated to the search results were forcibly popped up. The popping up of such advertisement pages was not caused by the programs installed on the computer of the notary office that accessed the Internet. China Unicom Qingdao Branch had neither evidence to prove that the same situation would occur within the network access service areas of other network access service providers, nor provided a reasonable explanation for the above situation that occurred within its own network access service area. Therefore, it should be held that the explanation provided by the plaintiff Baidu Inc. is established, namely, within the Internet access service area provided by China Unicom Qingdao Branch, there was human intervention in the search requests made by network service users to the Baidu website, causing the advertisement pages that the intervenor intended to publish to be forcibly popped up before the normal search results page appeared.

Regarding who is the subject implementing the above intervention, the introduction of the "Network Direct Express" ("网络直通车") service on the homepage of the defendant Aoshang Network Company shows that its description of the forcible popping up of advertisements is completely consistent in form with the notarized evidence preserved by the plaintiff Baidu Inc., and the popped-up advertisement pages "Bandao Talent Network" ("半岛人才网") and "114 Telephone Voice Search" ("114电话语音搜索") that appeared during the notarization and preservation are all websites or businesses that it is operating. Therefore, Aoshang Network Company is the beneficiary of this intervention. In the absence of evidence provided by it proving the existence of another subject that implemented the aforementioned advertising act for it, it should be held that Aoshang Network Company is the subject implementing the aforementioned intervention.

Although the defendant Aoshang Network Company is the subject implementing the above intervention, it does not mean that Aoshang Network Company is the sole subject of implementation. This intervention by Aoshang Network Company is not achieved by installing plug-ins, programs, or other means on the client computers, but can be realized within a specific network access service area. Therefore, this act cannot be accomplished without the cooperation of the network access service provider. The defendant China Unicom Qingdao Branch has no evidence to prove that Aoshang Network Company implemented the above act through illegal means to intervene in its Internet access service. Moreover, based on the facts ascertained in this case, the actual user of the domain name http://air.qd.sd.cn is China Unicom Qingdao Branch, and China Unicom Qingdao Branch and Aoshang Network Company cooperated in operating the telephone real-name business (电话实名业务). That is, China Unicom Qingdao Branch is also a beneficiary of the above act. Therefore, China Unicom Qingdao Branch is also a subject implementing the above intervention.

Regarding whether the defendant China Unicom Shandong Branch implemented the intervention, since China Unicom Shandong Branch and the defendant China Unicom Qingdao Branch are both branches of China United Network Communications Co., Ltd., the plaintiff Baidu Inc. has no evidence to prove that China Unicom Qingdao Branch was established and managed by China Unicom Shandong Branch, nor any evidence to prove that China Unicom Shandong Branch participated in the implementation of the intervention. As a civil subject, China Unicom Qingdao Branch has the capacity to bear civil liability. Therefore, the plaintiff's claims against China Unicom Shandong Branch are not supported. The plaintiff listed Pengfei Airlines as a third party in this case, but the plaintiff did not point out any unfair competition act by Pengfei Airlines in its complaint or during the court trial, nor did it request Pengfei Airlines to bear any civil liability. Therefore, the plaintiff's listing of Pengfei Airlines as a third party constitutes an improper enumeration of parties and is not supported.

II. Whether the Intervention Implemented by the Defendants Aoshang Network Company and China Unicom Qingdao Branch Constitutes Unfair Competition.

Chapter 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law) provides an enumerated list of unfair competition acts. For acts not specifically stipulated in the provisions, the court may apply the principle provisions of Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law for judgment and regulation. When making a judgment, the court should follow the following principle: for competitive acts not specifically regulated by law, they may only be determined as unfair competition if, according to generally accepted commercial standards and common understanding, they can be deemed to violate the principle provisions, so as to prevent hindering free and fair competition by improperly expanding the scope of unfair competition. To determine whether the above acts of the defendants China Unicom Qingdao Branch and Aoshang Network Company constitute unfair competition, the following elements must be satisfied: 1. The implementer of the act is an "operator" within the meaning of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law; 2. When engaging in commercial activities, the operator did not follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith, and violated generally accepted commercial ethics; 3. The operator's unfair competition act caused economic losses to the legitimate operator.

In this case, first, it should be clarified that the determination of an "operator" does not require the plaintiff and defendant to belong to the same industry or service category; any market entity engaged in commodity trading or for-profit services can be an operator. The defendant China Unicom Qingdao Branch and the defendant Aoshang Network Company are both market entities engaged in Internet-related businesses and are operators within the meaning of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Second, the way of publishing advertisements and conducting commercial activities on the Internet differs significantly from traditional business models. Through advanced computer network technology, commercial effects that are unattainable under traditional business models can be achieved. However, operators engaged in Internet-related businesses should still obtain corresponding profits or competitive advantages through honest operation and fair competition, and must not use others' services or market share for commercial operations and profit without their permission. In this case, the acts implemented by China Unicom Qingdao Branch and Aoshang Network Company took advantage of the fact that the Baidu website's search engine is widely used by Chinese Internet users. Using technical means, they caused network users who access the Internet through the Internet access service provided by China Unicom Qingdao Branch, when logging into the Baidu website for keyword searches, to have the advertisement pages published by Aoshang Network Company forcibly pop up before the normal search results are displayed. This act obviously uses the search service provided by the plaintiff Baidu Inc. for their own profit. This act was carried out without the consent of Baidu Inc., and also violates the will of the users of its Internet access service. It may easily lead network users to mistakenly believe that the popped-up advertisement pages are the act of Baidu Inc., thus potentially lowering the evaluation of the service provided by Baidu Inc. among network users and adversely affecting Baidu's commercial reputation.

In summary, the acts of the defendants China Unicom Qingdao Branch and Aoshang Network Company harmed the interests of the plaintiff Baidu Inc., violated the principle of good faith and generally accepted commercial ethics, and constituted unfair competition. They shall bear corresponding civil liability according to law.

Since the defendant China Unicom Qingdao Branch and the defendant Aoshang Network Company jointly implemented the unfair competition act, they shall bear joint and several liability in accordance with Article 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China. The specific methods of bearing civil liability, in accordance with Article 134 of the General Principles of the Civil Law and Article 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, shall include ceasing the infringement, compensating for losses, and eliminating the effects of the infringement. First, the two defendants shall immediately cease the unfair competition act, i.e., they shall not use technical means to cause network users who access the Internet through the Internet access service provided by China Unicom Qingdao Branch to have the defendants' advertisement pages pop up when logging into the Baidu website for keyword searches. Second, based on the above analysis, the acts of the two defendants caused economic losses to the plaintiff Baidu Inc. However, the plaintiff's claim for compensation of RMB 4,800,000 lacks legal and factual basis. Based on the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff for this case, the circumstances, duration, etc., of the defendants' unfair competition act, it is determined that the two defendants shall jointly compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of RMB 200,000. Finally, when Internet users log into Baidu for searches, they often believe that the popped-up advertisement pages are the act of Baidu Inc. Therefore, the acts of the two defendants caused certain negative impacts on the plaintiff, and they shall bear the civil liability of eliminating the effects. Since this act occurred on the Internet and within the Internet access service area provided by China Unicom Qingdao Branch, it is determined that the two defendants shall publish a statement to eliminate the effects on the homepage of their respective websites (Qingdao Information Port: www.qd.sd.cn, China Aoshang Network: www.og.com.cn). The content of the statement must be reviewed by the court, and the statement shall be published continuously for fifteen days.

In summary, the Qingdao Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 130 and Article 134 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 20 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, rendered the following judgment on September 2, 2009:

1. The defendants Aoshang Network Company and China Unicom Qingdao Branch shall immediately cease their unfair competition acts against the plaintiff Baidu Inc. from the effective date of this judgment, i.e., they shall not use technical means to cause network users who access the Internet through the Internet access service provided by China Unicom Qingdao Branch, when logging into the Baidu website for keyword searches, to have the advertisement pages of the two defendants pop up.

2. The defendants Aoshang Network Company and China Unicom Qingdao Branch shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiff Baidu Inc. for economic losses of RMB 200,000.

3. The defendants Aoshang Network Company and China Unicom Qingdao Branch shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, publish a statement on the homepage of their respective websites (Qingdao Information Port: www.qd.sd.cn, China Aoshang Network: www.og.com.cn) to eliminate the effects. The statement shall be published for a continuous period of 15 days, and its content must be reviewed by the court. If they fail to do so within the specified period, the court will publish the main contents of this judgment on relevant domestic portal websites, and the costs shall be borne jointly by the two defendants.

4. The other claims of the plaintiff Baidu Inc. are dismissed.

China Unicom Qingdao Branch, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Shandong High People's Court, requesting the revocation of the original judgment and a new judgment according to law. The main reasons are as follows: (1) The facts found in the first instance judgment are only a possibility, not a certainty. 1. The first instance judgment erroneously determined that the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch is the actual owner of the website http://air.qd.sd.cn. 2. The first instance judgment's determination that China Unicom Qingdao Branch is the subject implementing the alleged infringing act is illogical. (2) The first instance judgment erroneously found that China Unicom Qingdao Branch engaged in unfair competition. 1. The search engine service provided by the appellee Baidu Inc. is not a for-profit service and does not fall under the category of "operator" as defined in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law. Baidu Inc. does not have the standing to bring an unfair competition lawsuit in this case. 2. There is no competitive relationship between Baidu Inc. and China Unicom Qingdao Branch, and therefore an unfair competition lawsuit does not arise in this case.

The appellee Baidu Inc. argued in response: The first instance judgment clearly found the facts and correctly applied the law. The appeal grounds of the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch are not tenable. The appeal should be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

Upon second instance trial, the Shandong High People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The issues in dispute in this second instance trial are: 1. Whether the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch is the subject implementing the alleged unfair competition act; 2. Whether China Unicom Qingdao Branch engaged in unfair competition.

The Shandong High People's Court held in the second instance:

I. Regarding whether the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch is the subject implementing the alleged unfair competition act.

To determine whether the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch is the subject implementing the alleged unfair competition act, it is first necessary to confirm whether the involved website http://air.qd.sd.cn belongs to China Unicom Qingdao Branch. A domain name is a hierarchical character identifier for identifying and locating computers on the Internet. The involved domain name qd.sd.cn belongs to China Unicom Qingdao Branch and is actually used as the domain name for "Qingdao Information Port". As a subdomain of qd.sd.cn, air.qd.sd.cn is assigned and managed by its superior domain name qd.sd.cn. The holder of the domain name qd.sd.cn, China Unicom Qingdao Branch, denies that the domain name air.qd.sd.cn belongs to it, but did not provide evidence to prove this. The first instance judgment's finding that the user of this subdomain name at the time of the notarization and preservation by the appellee Baidu Inc. was China Unicom Qingdao Branch is not improper.

The alleged unfair competition act occurred in a specific Internet access service area. Original trial defendant Aoshang Network Company, as the subject implementing the alleged unfair competition act, could not have achieved the alleged unfair competition act without the cooperation of the Internet access service provider, in the absence of evidence proving that Aoshang Network Company intervened in the specific Internet access service through illegal means. At the same time, China Unicom Qingdao Branch is the owner of the domain name air.qd.sd.cn. Liability for infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of others due to holding or using a domain name shall be borne by the domain name holder. Therefore, the first instance court's determination that China Unicom Qingdao Branch is the subject implementing the alleged unfair competition act is not improper.

II. Regarding whether the defendant China Unicom Qingdao Branch engaged in unfair competition.

First, the appellee Baidu Inc. has standing to sue in this case. Baidu Inc. provides free web search services to ordinary Internet users on the one hand, and also provides paid search services and promotion services to enterprises and individuals on the other hand. When an Internet user inputs a keyword into the Baidu website for a search, the Baidu website will use its search engine to find and present page information related to the keyword, and at the same time, on the right side of the website, paid enterprise website links matching the keyword will appear. Therefore, Baidu Inc. is an operator within the meaning of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law and has standing to sue in this case.

Second, there is a competitive relationship between the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch and the appellee Baidu Inc., and China Unicom Qingdao Branch's act constitutes unfair competition.

Although the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch is an Internet access service operator and the appellee Baidu Inc. is a search service operator, and their service categories are not entirely the same, there is a competitive relationship between the commercial act implemented by China Unicom Qingdao Branch—popping up advertisements before Baidu search results appear—and Baidu's search model. According to the records in the involved notarized certificate, when searching for "鹏飞航空" (Pengfei Airlines) on the Baidu website, an advertisement page reading "For discounted air tickets, grab them now by dialing 114" popped up; when searching for "青岛人才网" (Qingdao Talent Network), an advertisement page reading "Looking for a good job, go to Bandao Talent Network www.job17.com" popped up; when searching for "电话实名" (telephone real-name), an advertisement page reading "Check information, dial 114, voice search is easier to use" popped up. It can be seen that the popped-up advertisements during the search are targeted and closely related to the searched keyword and content. China Unicom Qingdao Branch took advantage of the fact that the Baidu website's search engine is widely used by Chinese Internet users. Using technical means, it forcibly popped up advertisement pages it had placed, which were closely related to the searched keyword and content, before the Baidu search results appeared. This affected Baidu Inc.'s ability to provide search services and promotion services to network users according to its own will, and may also lead to the loss of search customers for the Baidu website. This constitutes an act of using the search service provided by Baidu Inc. to seek profit for itself. This act affected the service quality of Baidu Inc., harmed its legitimate interests, and may also lead Internet users to mistakenly believe that the popped-up advertisement pages are the act of Baidu Inc., thereby potentially lowering the evaluation of the service provided by Baidu Inc. among Internet users, adversely affecting Baidu's commercial reputation, and also violating the market conduct principles of honesty, good faith, and fair dealing, as well as generally accepted commercial ethics. Therefore, the first instance judgment's determination that the acts of China Unicom Qingdao Branch and original trial defendant Aoshang Network Company constituted unfair competition under Article 2 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law is not improper.

In summary, the appeal of the appellant China Unicom Qingdao Branch lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. The first instance judgment clearly found the facts and correctly applied the law, and should be affirmed. Accordingly, the Shandong High People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on March 20, 2010:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
